[BIS-CONSUMER-CARE] Consumer Protection, BIS Care App, HUID Verification & Penalties
BIS CARE Mobile Application Guide:
The official BIS CARE app (available on Android and iOS) empowers consumers to verify product genuineness before purchasing:
1. 'Verify Licence (CM/L)': Enter the 7 or 8-digit license number to view manufacturer name, brand, factory address, and validity status.
2. 'Verify R-Number': Check CRS registered electronics.
3. 'Verify HUID': Enter the 6-digit hallmark identifier on gold jewellery to confirm jeweller identity and hallmarking date.
title: Consumer Protection, BIS Care App, HUID Verification & Penalties

text:
[BIS-CONSUMER-CARE] Consumer Protection, BIS Care App, HUID Verification & Penalties
Filing Complaints & Grievance Redressal:
Consumers can file complaints regarding: (a) Misuse of ISI mark without a valid license, (b) Substandard certified products that failed during use, (c) False or counterfeit gold hallmarking. Complaints can be lodged via BIS CARE App ('Complaints' tab), on the portal 'www.bis.gov.in', or by calling the National Consumer Helpline at 1915. Complainants receive a unique tracking token.
title: Consumer Protection, BIS Care App, HUID Verification & Penalties

text:
[BIS-CONSUMER-CARE] Consumer Protection, BIS Care App, HUID Verification & Penalties
Statutory Penalties Under Section 29 of BIS Act 2016:
Section 29 of the BIS Act 2016 provides stringent criminal penalties for the misuse of standard marks or manufacturing notified mandatory goods without certification:
- Imprisonment for a term up to two years, OR
- A fine not less than ₹2,00,000 (Rupees Two Lakh), which may extend up to ten times the value of products manufactured or sold, OR both.
- Search and seizure of illegal stock is conducted by BIS Enforcement Branch with police assistance.

text:
[BIS-LAB-DIRECTORY] BIS Central, Regional & Branch Laboratories Directory and Testing Scope
CPRI (Central Power Research Institute) Testing Scope & Submission:
Central Power Research Institute (CPRI), Sir C.V. Raman Road, Sadashivanagar, P.B. No. 8066, Bengaluru 560080 (and regional units in Bhopal, Hyderabad, Nagpur, Noida, Kolkata).
Disciplines & Testing Scope: Short-circuit testing, high-voltage transformers (IS 1180), switchgear & controlgear, lightning arresters, electric vehicle (EV) supply equipment & chargers, power cables, and smart meters.
How to Submit Product Test Samples to CPRI:
1. Obtain a Test Request Form (TRF) or Manakonline Application Reference Number from BIS if applying under BIS Product Certification / CRS Scheme.
2. Fill out the CPRI Testing Requisition Form available on the CPRI customer portal (www.cpri.res.in), specifying the applicable Indian Standard (IS code) and test parameters required.
3. Securely pack product test samples with tamper-evident seals and attach official identification labels stating sample manufacturer, batch number, ratings, and BIS application ID.
4. Deliver or courier the sample to the CPRI Central Reception / Customer Service Cell along with the advance testing fee and manufacturer test certificate (MTC).
5. Following testing, CPRI issues an accredited test report and uploads it electronically to the BIS Manakonline portal for grant of license or CRS approval.

[BIS-LAB-DIRECTORY] BIS Central, Regional & Branch Laboratories Directory and Testing Scope
Sample Submission Guidelines to BIS Recognized Laboratories:
Protocol for Submitting Product Samples for BIS Conformity Testing:
1. Preliminary Application: The applicant must have a valid application registered on Manakonline (www.manakonline.in) for Scheme I (ISI Mark) or Scheme II (CRS).
2. Sample Drawing & Counter-Sealing: Under Normal Procedure, samples are drawn during factory audit by the BIS inspecting officer and counter-sealed. Under Simplified Procedure / Option 2, the manufacturer submits self-drawn samples directly to an LRS recognized lab before audit.
3. Documentation: Each sample consignment must include: (a) BIS Test Request Form (TRF), (b) Copy of Form I application, (c) Detailed technical construction file (TCF) / circuit diagram, (d) Payment receipt of prescribed testing charges.
4. Receipt & Witnessing: Lab acknowledges receipt on the portal. Manufacturer may request to witness non-destructive tests where permissible under standard guidelines.

[BIS-PROCESS-GUIDE] Step-by-Step Guide to Applying for a BIS License & Fee Structure
Step 1 & 2: Identification & Online Filing:
Step 1: Identify the relevant Indian Standard (IS code) and product manual on the BIS website.
Step 2: Register on the online portal 'www.manakonline.in'. Submit Form I application with factory address, manufacturing machinery list, testing equipment calibration certificates, and raw material test reports. Pay non-refundable application fee of ₹1,000.
title: Step-by-Step Guide to Applying for a BIS License & Fee Structure

metadata.title: Step-by-Step Guide to Applying for a BIS License & Fee Structure

text:
[BIS-PROCESS-GUIDE] Step-by-Step Guide to Applying for a BIS License & Fee Structure
Step 3 & 4: Factory Audit & Sample Testing:
Step 3: A designated BIS technical officer conducts a physical or hybrid inspection of the manufacturing premises to verify manufacturing capability, quality control personnel, in-house lab, and Scheme of Inspection and Testing (SIT).
Step 4: The officer draws independent test samples, seals them, and dispatches them to a BIS Central/Regional lab or NABL referral lab for conformity testing.
title: Step-by-Step Guide to Applying for a BIS License & Fee Structure

text:
[BIS-PROCESS-GUIDE] Step-by-Step Guide to Applying for a BIS License & Fee Structure
Step 5: Grant of License & Marking Fee Structure:
Step 5: Once lab test results indicate full conformity, BIS issues the Certificate of Manufacturing License (CM/L number). Licensee pays the annual license fee (₹1,000) plus the applicable minimum advance marking fee (ranges from ₹10,000 to ₹1,00,000 depending on product class and production volume).

[BIS-SCHEMES-2024] Compendium of BIS Product Certification Schemes & Conformity Assessment
Scheme I — ISI Product Certification Scheme:
Scheme I is the flagship certification system of BIS. It covers over 1,000 products, granting manufacturers the right to use the coveted ISI mark. Process involves: application submission -> factory preliminary audit by BIS technical auditor -> drawing of independent samples -> rigorous testing in NABL/BIS lab -> grant of CM/L license. Licenses are valid for 1 to 2 years, renewable upon payment of marking fees.

text:
[BIS-SCHEMES-2024] Compendium of BIS Product Certification Schemes & Conformity Assessment
Scheme II — Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS):
Introduced by MeitY and BIS for electronics, IT hardware, solar equipment, and smart devices (60+ product categories including laptops, mobile phones, LED lights, power banks, and servers). Manufacturers get their product tested at BIS-approved laboratories and apply online on the CRS portal. No factory audit is conducted prior to registration; renewal is every 2 years.

text:
[BIS-SCHEMES-2024] Compendium of BIS Product Certification Schemes & Conformity Assessment
Scheme IV — Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme (FMCS):
Enables overseas manufacturing units located outside India to obtain an ISI mark for goods shipped into India. Foreign applicant must appoint an Authorized Indian Representative (AIR) residing in India, pay audit charges for two BIS auditors to inspect the overseas factory, and maintain local laboratory testing facilities.

text:
[IS 10500:2012] Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision)
1.0 Scope:
This standard prescribes the quality requirements and methods of sampling and test for drinking water (piped water supplies, packaged drinking water, water from public wells, borewells, and tankers). It sets limits for physical, chemical, and bacteriological parameters to ensure the water is wholesome and safe for domestic human consumption.
title: Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision)

metadata.title: Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision)

text:
[IS 10500:2012] Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision)
Table 1 — Physical & Organoleptic Parameters:
Requirements for physical characteristics of drinking water:
- Colour: Acceptable limit 5 Hazen units max; Permissible limit in the absence of alternate source is 15 Hazen units max.
- Odour: Agreeable.
- Taste: Agreeable.
- Turbidity: Acceptable limit 1 NTU max; Permissible limit in the absence of alternate source is 5 NTU max.
- pH Value: Acceptable range 6.5 to 8.5; No relaxation.
- Total Dissolved Solids (TDS): Acceptable limit 500 mg/L max; Permissible limit in the absence of alternate source is 2000 mg/L max.
title: Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision)

metadata.title: Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision)

text:
[IS 10500:2012] Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision)
Table 2 — General Chemical & Toxic Parameters:
Limits for general chemical and toxic substances:
- Total Hardness (as CaCO3): Acceptable limit 200 mg/L max; Permissible limit 600 mg/L max.
- Chlorides (as Cl): Acceptable limit 250 mg/L max; Permissible limit 1000 mg/L max.
- Fluoride (as F): Acceptable limit 1.0 mg/L max; Permissible limit 1.5 mg/L max. Excess fluoride causes dental and skeletal fluorosis.
- Nitrate (as NO3): Acceptable limit 45 mg/L max; No relaxation. Higher levels cause methaemoglobinaemia (blue baby disease).
- Iron (as Fe): Acceptable limit 0.3 mg/L max; Permissible limit 1.0 mg/L max.
- Lead (as Pb): Maximum permissible limit 0.01 mg/L max; No relaxation (toxic heavy metal).
- Arsenic (as As): Maximum limit 0.01 mg/L max; Permissible limit 0.05 mg/L max.
title: Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision)

metadata.title: Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision)

text:
[IS 10500:2012] Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision)
Table 6 — Microbiological Requirements:
All water intended for human consumption:
- E. coli or thermotolerant coliform bacteria must not be detectable in any 100 ml sample.
- Total coliform bacteria must not be detectable in any 100 ml sample of treated piped water supply.
- If coliforms are detected, immediate sanitary survey and repeat testing is mandatory.

text:
[IS 1417:2016] Gold and Gold Alloys, Platinum & Silver — Hallmarking Specification
1.0 Mandatory Gold Hallmarking Scope:
Under the Hallmarking of Gold Jewellery and Gold Artefacts Order, sale of hallmarked gold jewellery is mandatory across notified districts in India. Jewellers selling un-hallmarked gold jewellery are liable to penalties under Section 29 of the BIS Act, including seizure of stock and fines up to five times the value of the article.
title: Gold and Gold Alloys, Platinum & Silver — Hallmarking Specification

metadata.title: Gold and Gold Alloys, Platinum & Silver — Hallmarking Specification

text:
[IS 1417:2016] Gold and Gold Alloys, Platinum & Silver — Hallmarking Specification
Clause 4.1 Permitted Purity Grades:
Gold jewellery hallmarking is permitted strictly in six designated purity grades:
- 24K: 995 parts per thousand (99.5% pure gold)
- 23K: 958 parts per thousand (95.8% pure gold)
- 22K: 916 parts per thousand (91.6% pure gold — most common for traditional jewellery)
- 20K: 833 parts per thousand (83.3% pure gold)
- 18K: 750 parts per thousand (75.0% pure gold — diamond-studded jewellery)
- 14K: 585 parts per thousand (58.5% pure gold — lightweight modern jewellery).
title: Gold and Gold Alloys, Platinum & Silver — Hallmarking Specification

metadata.title: Gold and Gold Alloys, Platinum & Silver — Hallmarking Specification

text:
[IS 1417:2016] Gold and Gold Alloys, Platinum & Silver — Hallmarking Specification
Clause 5.0 Three Mandatory Marks on Gold Jewellery:
Every genuine hallmarked gold article contains exactly three indelible laser marks:
1. The BIS Triangular Logo (signifying national standards guarantee)
2. Purity Fineness mark (e.g., '22K916' or '18K750')
3. 6-digit alphanumeric Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID) code (e.g., 'AB12C3').
Consumers can input this 6-digit code into the BIS CARE mobile app to verify the jeweller's registration, assaying center (AHC), date of hallmarking, and article type.
clause: Clause 5.0 Three Mandatory Marks on Gold Jewellery
title: Gold and Gold Alloys, Platinum & Silver — Hallmarking Specification

[IS 1417:2016] Gold and Gold Alloys, Platinum & Silver — Hallmarking Specification
Silver Hallmarking Status:
Silver hallmarking is currently VOLUNTARY in India under IS 2112:2014. Standard fineness grades for silver are 999 (fine silver), 970, 925 (Sterling Silver), 900, 835, and 800. Hallmarking of silver is performed by BIS-recognized AHCs upon jeweller request.

[IS 16102 (Part 1 & 2):2012] Self-Ballasted LED Lamps for General Lighting Services
Part 1 — Safety Requirements:
Self-ballasted LED lamps for voltages up to 250V AC/DC fall under the Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS, Scheme II). Safety requirements cover: insulation resistance, electric strength (withstand 4000V high-pot test), mechanical resistance to torque, flame retardancy of lamp cap, and protection against accidental electric shock.
title: Self-Ballasted LED Lamps for General Lighting Services

metadata.title: Self-Ballasted LED Lamps for General Lighting Services

text:
[IS 16102 (Part 1 & 2):2012] Self-Ballasted LED Lamps for General Lighting Services
Part 2 — Performance & Energy Efficiency:
Specifies photometric performance: luminous efficacy must not be less than 90 lumens/watt for cool daylight lamps; power factor must be greater than 0.90 for ratings above 5W to prevent grid distortion; colour rendering index (CRI) Ra >= 80; lumen maintenance at 2,000 hours must exceed 90% of rated initial lumen output.
title: Self-Ballasted LED Lamps for General Lighting Services

metadata.title: Self-Ballasted LED Lamps for General Lighting Services

text:
[IS 16102 (Part 1 & 2):2012] Self-Ballasted LED Lamps for General Lighting Services
CRS Self-Declaration Mark:
Unlike Scheme I (ISI Mark), products certified under CRS display the words 'Self-Declaration - Conforming to IS 16102 (Part 1)' along with the standard BIS Registration symbol and unique 8-digit R-number (e.g., R-41012345). No factory inspection is required prior to grant; registration is granted purely on valid test reports from BIS-recognized labs.

text:
[IS 2347:2017] Domestic Pressure Cookers — Specification (Fifth Revision)
1.0 Scope & Mandatory Status:
Domestic pressure cookers sold, imported, or manufactured in India MUST mandatorily carry the Standard ISI Mark under the Domestic Pressure Cookers (Quality Control) Order. Manufacturing or selling uncertified domestic pressure cookers without a valid BIS CM/L license is a criminal offense under Section 16 & 29 of the BIS Act 2016.
title: Domestic Pressure Cookers — Specification (Fifth Revision)

metadata.title: Domestic Pressure Cookers — Specification (Fifth Revision)

text:
[IS 2347:2017] Domestic Pressure Cookers — Specification (Fifth Revision)
Clause 4.1 Materials & Construction:
Pressure cooker bodies and lids must be made of food-grade wrought aluminium alloy (IS 21), stainless steel (AISI 304 / Grade 18/8), or composite metals. Minimum body thickness for aluminium is 3.25 mm; for stainless steel it is 1.0 mm to prevent thermal distortion and violent rupture.
title: Domestic Pressure Cookers — Specification (Fifth Revision)

metadata.title: Domestic Pressure Cookers — Specification (Fifth Revision)

text:
[IS 2347:2017] Domestic Pressure Cookers — Specification (Fifth Revision)
Clause 6.3 Safety Devices & Bursting Pressure Test:
Every cooker must have a primary pressure regulating weight vent (operates at 1.0 kgf/cm² ± 0.1) and a secondary fusible safety plug/valve that fuses between 1.4 to 2.0 kgf/cm² if the main vent gets blocked. The hydrostatic proof pressure test requires the cooker to withstand 2.5 times the operating pressure without leakage or permanent deformation.
clause: Clause 6.3 Safety Devices & Bursting Pressure Test
title: Domestic Pressure Cookers — Specification (Fifth Revision)

metadata.clause: Clause 6.3 Safety Devices & Bursting Pressure Test

text:
[IS 2347:2017] Domestic Pressure Cookers — Specification (Fifth Revision)
Clause 9.0 Marking Requirements:
Every cooker must be indelibly stamped on its bottom with: (a) Manufacturer's name or trademark, (b) Nominal capacity in litres, (c) Standard Mark (ISI logo), (d) 7 or 8-digit BIS License Number (CM/L-XXXXXXXX), and (e) Batch number and month/year of manufacture.
